judged_text: updateEvent's fallback predicate event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares every calendar's externalId against null/undefined and can never match, leaving selectedCalendar undefined where the old code returned destinationCalendar.externalId. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback `selectedCalendar` is now computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. This fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but then it compares each `cal.externalId` to that falsy `externalCalendarId` (null/undefined), so it will not find the intended calendar and yields `undefined` (where the old code returned `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`). Unlike `createEvent` (which defaults to `"primary"`), `updateEvent` does not apply a default and will call `calendar.events.update` with an undefined `calendarId`, which matches the reported broken behavior. The diff also shows paths that can produce missing `externalCalendarId` references (e.g., `createAllCalendarEvents` calling `createEvent(c, event)` without the new `externalId` argument), making this failure reachable.
